inputs.products: Millet-based chips and cookies made in Hyderabad. No maida, no palm oil. Sold on our website and Instagram. Launching a Snack Box sampler with 6 flavours.
inputs.instructions: Use Hinglish sparingly. Never mention competitors.

voice_summary: Warm, playful snack talk with a light desi flavour.
Lead with the six-flavour Snack Box as an easy, inviting way to sample the range.
Make clear product truths—millet-based, no maida and no palm oil—feel appetising rather than clinical.
Use mostly English, adding Hinglish sparingly and naturally.

tone.detail: Sound like a friendly host offering a tasty snack, using welcoming language rather than a hard sell.
Use light wordplay, snack-time observations and flavour-led phrasing without becoming loud or chaotic.
Add occasional familiar Indian expressions or cultural cues, while keeping Hinglish sparse and easy to understand.
State the product differentiators simply—millet-based, no maida and no palm oil—then return the focus to enjoyment.

target_audience.description: Health-conscious Indian snack buyers who shop online, enjoy discovering new flavours and want convenient alternatives to conventional chips and cookies.

content_themes.detail: Promote the sampler as a convenient way to discover six flavours in one box.
Spotlight the variety inside the Snack Box through flavour reveals, rankings, polls and pick-your-favourite prompts, without inventing flavour names.
Explain that the chips and cookies are millet-based in short, accessible, appetite-forward language.
Turn these product facts into concise promotional proof points without making unsupported health claims.
Place the products in relatable moments such as chai breaks, desk cravings, evening munchies and sharing at home.
Encourage audiences to explore and order through the brand website or Instagram.

brand_hooks.hook: Millet-based chips and cookies made in Hyderabad.
Products made without maida or palm oil.
A Snack Box sampler containing six flavours.
Available directly through the brand website and Instagram.

style_rules.language: Primarily English with occasional, simple Hinglish
style_rules.sentence_style: Short, conversational sentences with appetising product language, clear benefits and a gentle promotional call to action.
signature_patterns: Open with a relatable snack craving or moment, then introduce the product.
Use a playful either-or question or poll around flavours and snack preferences.
Pair one product truth with one appetite cue: millet-based, crunchy and ready for snack time.
Close with a simple invitation to discover or order the six-flavour Snack Box.

dos: Make the Snack Box and its six-flavour variety the centre of launch posts.
Balance product credentials with sensory, enjoyable snack language.
Use Hyderabad as a genuine point of origin when relevant.
Keep Hinglish occasional, familiar and understandable from context.
Use clear calls to action directing people to the website or Instagram.
donts: Do not mention or allude to competitors.
Do not invent flavour names, nutritional values, prices, discounts or availability details.
Do not imply that no maida or no palm oil automatically makes the products medically healthy.
Do not overload posts with Hinglish, slang, emojis or hashtags.
Do not sound preachy, restrictive or guilt-driven about snacking.
assumptions: The target audience is inferred because no age, geography or customer profile was supplied.
Everyday occasions such as chai breaks, desk cravings and evening snacking are suggested content contexts, not stated brand claims.
Light emoji and hashtag use are defaults because no past posts or research were available to establish an existing pattern.
The voice should remain primarily English because the user requested that Hinglish be used sparingly.
No individual flavour names, prices, launch date or offer mechanics were provided, so posts should not add them.

tweets.text: Meet six flavours without committing to just one. Our Hyderabad-made Snack Box brings millet-based chips and cookies together, with no maida and no palm oil. Find your favourite on our website.
tweets.why: Leads with the six-flavour sampler and clear product truths.

tweets.text: Chai-time decision: open a flavour from the Snack Box now, or save all six for an evening tasting session? Batao 👇
tweets.why: Uses the six-flavour Snack Box in a playful, lightly desi choice.

tweets.text: POV: You opened the six-flavour Snack Box “just to see what’s inside” and accidentally started a full Hyderabad millet-snack tasting.
tweets.why: Uses a meme format with the Hyderabad-made six-flavour sampler.

tweets.text: Hosting tip: put out small bowls for each of the six Snack Box flavours, then let everyone rank their picks. It makes tasting—and finding a millet-based favourite—much easier.
tweets.why: Turns the six-flavour sampler into a practical tasting activity.

tweets.text: Desk craving at 4? Keep the six-flavour Snack Box nearby for millet-based chips and cookies made without maida or palm oil. Order yours through Instagram.
tweets.why: Places the Snack Box in a relatable snack moment with a direct CTA.

tweets.text: Fill in the blank: My first pick from a six-flavour Hyderabad-made Snack Box would always be the one that tastes ______.
tweets.why: Invites flavour discovery while highlighting Hyderabad origin and six choices.

tweets.angle: wordplay on the product or category
tweets.text: Millet us be honest: choosing one favourite from six flavours is serious snack business. Good thing the Snack Box understands commitment issues.
tweets.why: Uses millet wordplay around the six-flavour sampler.

tweets.text: Build a simple Snack Box tasting: 1) Open one flavour at a time. 2) Pair the chips or cookies with your usual chai break. 3) Note which of the six earns a repeat opening.
tweets.why: Offers a useful three-step way to sample the six flavours.

tweets.why: Spotlights only the brand’s stated differentiators and origin.

tweets.originalText: Curious about our millet-based chips and cookies? Start with one box, six flavours and plenty of tasting possibilities. Message us on Instagram to try the Snack Box.
